AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is compost manure? (1 mark)
   A. Fertiliser made in a factory
   B. Fresh soil from a river bank
   C. A dark crumbly material made when plant and animal wastes rot
   D. A kind of animal feed

2. Which of these is a green material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Straw
   B. Fresh cut grass
   C. Dry maize stalks
   D. Dry leaves

3. How can compost be used in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Feed it to fish
   B. Throw it away
   C. Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops
   D. Use it to build a wall

4. What should you do if a hole in a drip pipe is blocked? (1 mark)
   A. Throw away the whole system
   B. Pour hot oil in it
   C. Clear it gently with a thin wire
   D. Cut the pipe in half

5. Which pupil is saving water? (1 mark)
   A. One who pours buckets over the whole bed
   B. One who leaves the tap running
   C. One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   D. One who waters at midday

6. Where should kerosene be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   B. In a water bottle on the table
   C. Near the fire
   D. In an open bowl

7. Why is wet firewood a poor fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It lasts forever
   B. It has no smoke
   C. It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
   D. It burns very hot

8. Why is dry firewood better than wet firewood? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot burn
   B. It is heavier
   C. It puts out fires
   D. It burns better with less smoke

9. How long may carrot seeds take to sprout? (1 mark)
   A. One year
   B. One to three weeks
   C. One day
   D. One hour

10. Why should young fruit trees be watered in dry weather? (1 mark)
   A. They do not need water
   B. Their roots are small and cannot reach much water
   C. Water kills them
   D. Water makes fruit sour

11. What is a fruit? (1 mark)
   A. The roots of a plant
   B. The part of a plant that holds the seeds
   C. The leaves of a plant
   D. The stem of a plant

12. Which of these is a fruit crop? (1 mark)
   A. Guava
   B. Sukuma wiki
   C. Cabbage
   D. Spinach

13. What is topsoil? (1 mark)
   A. The bottom layer
   B. Sand from the river
   C. The dark top layer of soil
   D. A fertiliser

14. What is a trellis? (1 mark)
   A. A support structure for climbing plants
   B. A bag for seeds
   C. A type of fruit
   D. A tool for cutting

15. Why is mulch put around a young tree? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the tree shorter
   B. It kills roots
   C. It stops flowering
   D. It keeps the soil moist and controls weeds

16. Where should the graft joint of a grafted seedling be? (1 mark)
   A. Deep below the soil
   B. Above the ground
   C. In water
   D. In the compost

17. Who should be called when a cow is sick? (1 mark)
   A. A veterinary officer
   B. A tailor
   C. A driver
   D. A carpenter

18. How does manure from animals help crops? (1 mark)
   A. It gives shade
   B. It makes crops small
   C. It scares birds
   D. It supplies plant food to the soil

19. What is meant by income from animals? (1 mark)
   A. Manure used
   B. Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   C. Food eaten at home
   D. Feathers

20. Which group of animals is called poultry? (1 mark)
   A. Zebras and giraffes
   B. Sheep and goats
   C. Chickens, ducks and turkeys
   D. Cows and bulls

21. What is the young one of a sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Foal
   B. Kid
   C. Lamb
   D. Calf

22. Which product comes from a hen? (1 mark)
   A. Wool
   B. Honey
   C. Eggs
   D. Leather

23. Which food is a good source of protein and cheap in many homes? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Beans
   C. Sugar
   D. Soda

24. Which of these can happen if a child eats only ugali? (1 mark)
   A. Getting all vitamins
   B. Never feeling tired
   C. Feeling weak and getting sick often
   D. Growing very tall at once

25. Which local vegetable is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Butter
   B. Managu
   C. Ugali
   D. Rice

26. Which activity is part of keeping a food journal? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking only
   B. Buying food
   C. Throwing food away
   D. Writing what you eat at each meal

27. How much oil is used for shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. A full pot
   B. A whole bottle
   C. A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
   D. None

28. What is the first thing to do with leftover cooked food? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it in the sun
   B. Cover it and store it safely
   C. Leave it on the floor
   D. Throw it in the road

29. What should be done with a fire after cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Cover it with paper
   B. Put it out or switch off the gas
   C. Add more wood
   D. Leave it burning

30. Why should we wear shoes? (1 mark)
   A. To protect feet from injury, worms and jiggers
   B. To hide our feet
   C. To be heavier
   D. To make us tall

31. Why should you wash hands after removing gloves? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves are heavy
   B. Gloves are wet
   C. To dry the gloves
   D. Hands may still have germs

32. Why should you not dip hands into a drinking water container? (1 mark)
   A. Hands may put germs into the water
   B. The container would break
   C. The water would evaporate
   D. Hands would get cold

33. Which of these can be made into a mop? (1 mark)
   A. A chair
   B. Strips of old cloth tied to a stick
   C. A basin
   D. A shoe

34. What should you do after mopping a floor? (1 mark)
   A. Run on it
   B. Sweep it
   C. Put up a sign that the floor is wet
   D. Pour more water

35. Which PPE is worn on the feet at school and in the garden? (1 mark)
   A. Overall
   B. Gloves
   C. Canvas shoes
   D. Dust mask

36. Which PPE keeps dust from being breathed in? (1 mark)
   A. Headgear
   B. Overall
   C. Dust mask
   D. Gumboots

37. Why should PPE be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Dirty PPE can carry germs
   B. To make it smell
   C. Clean PPE is heavier
   D. Dirty PPE lasts longer

38. What should you do with tacking when permanent sewing is done? (1 mark)
   A. Wash it
   B. Dye it
   C. Leave it for ever
   D. Cut and pull it out

39. How long should a length of thread be for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. About as long as from fingertips to elbow, up to 50 cm
   B. 1 cm
   C. As long as the room
   D. 10 metres

40. Which is a type of tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. Even tacking
   B. Chain stitch
   C. Cross stitch
   D. Satin stitch

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Why should you brush teeth twice a day? (2 marks)

42. Name three foods that can be shallow fried. (3 marks)

43. Describe how to make long and short tacking. (4 marks)

44. Why do we need protective foods? (2 marks)

45. Give three uses of chickens. (3 marks)

46. Describe how to boil potatoes. (4 marks)

47. How can a school without land grow radish or amaranth? (3 marks)

48. State the functions of roots, leaves and flowers in a fruit tree. (3 marks)

49. Name three products we get from cattle. (3 marks)

50. Explain how to look after a compost heap for two months. (4 marks)

51. Give three times when you should wash your hands. (3 marks)

52. Why should fruit be washed before it is eaten? (2 marks)

53. Give three reasons why fruits are important. (3 marks)

54. Design a hygiene log for one week. List five practices to record and explain how you will use it. (5 marks)

55. Explain the difference between green and brown materials for compost, with an example of each. (3 marks)

56. Describe how to mop a floor. (4 marks)

57. Explain why tacking thread should be loose. (2 marks)

58. Name the three main food groups and one example of each. (3 marks)

59. Why should a thread colour different from the cloth be used? (2 marks)

60. Give two ways of protecting fruits from birds and monkeys without killing them. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — A dark crumbly material made when plant and animal wastes rot
   Compost is organic manure made from rotted wastes.

2. B — Fresh cut grass
   Green materials are fresh and wet, such as fresh grass, peelings and fresh dung.

3. C — Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops
   Compost feeds crops and improves the soil.

4. C — Clear it gently with a thin wire
   A thin wire clears blockages without damaging the pipe.

5. C — One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   Drip watering is the most water-saving.

6. A — In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   Kerosene catches fire easily and is poisonous.

7. C — It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
   Wet wood wastes heat drying itself.

8. D — It burns better with less smoke
   Dry wood gives more heat and less smoke.

9. B — One to three weeks
   Carrot seeds are slow, so be patient.

10. B — Their roots are small and cannot reach much water
   Young trees are easily stressed by drought.

11. B — The part of a plant that holds the seeds
   Fruits grow from flowers and hold seeds.

12. A — Guava
   Guava is a fruit.

13. C — The dark top layer of soil
   Topsoil is rich in plant food.

14. A — A support structure for climbing plants
   A trellis is posts and wires to hold climbers.

15. D — It keeps the soil moist and controls weeds
   Mulch reduces evaporation.

16. B — Above the ground
   Buried joints can rot or grow roots of the wrong kind.

17. A — A veterinary officer
   A vet treats sick animals.

18. D — It supplies plant food to the soil
   Manure enriches the soil.

19. B — Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   Farmers sell products to earn money.

20. C — Chickens, ducks and turkeys
   Poultry means birds kept for eggs and meat.

21. C — Lamb
   A young sheep is a lamb.

22. C — Eggs
   Hens lay eggs.

23. B — Beans
   Beans are protein-rich.

24. C — Feeling weak and getting sick often
   One food cannot supply all nutrients.

25. B — Managu
   Managu is a green leafy vegetable.

26. D — Writing what you eat at each meal
   Records help you check your meals.

27. C — A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
   Shallow frying uses a thin layer.

28. B — Cover it and store it safely
   Covered food stays safe from flies.

29. B — Put it out or switch off the gas
   This prevents accidents and saves fuel.

30. A — To protect feet from injury, worms and jiggers
   Shoes protect the feet.

31. D — Hands may still have germs
   Germs can get on hands.

32. A — Hands may put germs into the water
   Use a clean cup or tap.

33. B — Strips of old cloth tied to a stick
   A cloth mop works well.

34. C — Put up a sign that the floor is wet
   Wet floors are slippery.

35. C — Canvas shoes
   Canvas shoes protect feet.

36. C — Dust mask
   A mask covers the nose and mouth.

37. A — Dirty PPE can carry germs
   Clean PPE is safe and lasts longer.

38. D — Cut and pull it out
   Tacking is temporary.

39. A — About as long as from fingertips to elbow, up to 50 cm
   Long thread tangles.

40. A — Even tacking
   Even tacking is taught in Grade 4.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: It removes food and germs that cause decay and keeps the mouth fresh.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for removing food, 1 mark for preventing decay.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eggs, fish, sausages, onions, chapati (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mark a line; make a long stitch of about 2 cm on top; make a short stitch of about 0.5 cm underneath; repeat along the line; finish with a small back stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals that fight sickness and keep the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fight sickness, 1 mark for vitamins or minerals.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eggs, meat, manure, feathers and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash, peel and cut into equal pieces; put in a pot with water and salt; cover and boil for about 15 to 20 minutes until soft; drain the water carefully.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a box or tin with drainage holes filled with fine soil and compost; sow the seeds thinly; water gently and place in sunlight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for container, sowing, care.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the tree and take in water; leaves make food using sunlight; flowers form fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Milk, beef, hides and skins, manure, or draught power (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each product.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Keep it damp like a squeezed sponge, keep it covered, turn it after two to three weeks, and keep children and animals away.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct care activity, up to 4.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before eating, after using the toilet, after playing outside, after touching animals, after coughing (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remove dirt and germs so it is safe to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for germs or safety.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins, they give fibre and water, and they can be sold for money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Practices: washed hands before meals, brushed teeth twice, bathed, clean clothes, drank safe water. Tick each day, count ticks at the end, and improve the practice with fewest ticks.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for practices and table, 2 marks for use.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Green materials are fresh and wet such as fresh grass or peelings. Brown materials are dry such as dry leaves or straw.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sweep first; fill a bucket with clean soapy water; squeeze the mop; start from the far corner and mop backwards to the door; rinse the mop; leave the floor to dry with a warning.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Tight thread pulls and wrinkles the cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for pulls, 1 mark for wrinkles.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy-giving: ugali; body-building: beans; protective: sukuma wiki (or other correct examples).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with example.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: The stitches are easy to see and to remove.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Cover with nets, use scarecrows, noise or shiny objects (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
